title: Batch coordinated throttle wave investigation and hardening
creator: Asha Patel
description: During a sustained traffic increase on a Dedicated cluster, we observed repeating ~30s windows where continuous batching produced almost no batches for high-priority routes, causing tail latency spikes and uneven fairness across tenants. This ticket captures the post-incident investigation, root cause analysis, and concrete hardening tasks to prevent recurrence.
incident_summary: At 2026-03-03 14:21 UTC a coordinated throttle wave originated from autoscaler+maintenance interactions. Request pacing and deferred token replenishment caused the batcher to repeatedly skip forming windows for ~30 second intervals. High-priority requests that relied on continuous coalescing experienced tail P95-99 latency spikes (2-6x) and some tenant-level unfairness where low QPS-but-long requests consumed coalescer attention.
timeline: 2026-03-03 14:12 UTC - Gradual traffic ramp in region-us-west; 14:21 UTC - Metric spike and first customer alert; 14:22-14:48 UTC - Repeating batch silence windows observed; 14:30 UTC - Ops mitigation: temporarily reduced min_throughput on autoscaler; 15:05 UTC - Traffic normalization; 16:00 UTC - Initial blameless postmortem triage
root_cause: Interaction between three systems: (1) Autoscaler heartbeat batching that synchronized throttled token updates across hosts, (2) a maintenance task that deferred background KV eviction for 30s windows, and (3) a pacing heuristic in the coalescer that backoffed aggressively when observed slot contention. Combined, these caused intermittent batch formation suppression for priority routes. No single change was solely responsible; the failure mode is an emergent timing interaction.
mitigations: Short-term: revert aggressive coalescer backoff (rolled back), add alerting on consecutive empty-batch windows, and apply a temporary jitter to autoscaler token updates. Medium-term: introduce a small 'fast-path' to form batches for high-priority short requests even if the coalescer is in backoff; ensure maintenance tasks yield to request-critical paths. Long-term: implement a probabilistic jitter in all control-plane heartbeats and a formal 'batch silence' SLO with automated remediation.

postmortem_notes: We confirmed the emergent timing interaction in a reproducible test harness. Reverting the backoff change alone reduced but did not eliminate the windows — the combination with synchronized autoscaler heartbeats was necessary for full reproduction. Priority fast-paths significantly reduce observed tail latency in load tests. We will treat synchronized control-plane waves as first-class failure modes in future capacity tests.
review_comments: PM: prioritize fast-path for customer-impacting routes. SRE: require alert on 3 consecutive empty-batch windows. Design: ensure fast-path maintains isolation between tenants. Security: no secrets exposure; KMS unaffected.
verification_plan: 1) Unit tests for jittered heartbeat behavior. 2) Staging chaos run that synchronizes autoscaler heartbeats + maintenance deferral for 30m and validates no empty-batch windows >10s. 3) Gradual canary rollout of fast-path on 10% of hosts with telemetry checks. 4) Post-deployment: monitor P95/P99 for priority routes for 72h.
customer_communication: Customer-facing incident summary prepared and slated for release to affected customers by 2026-03-13. Incident describes cause, mitigations applied, and roadmap to harden the coalescer and autoscaler interaction.
notes: Avoid changing batching heuristics without a staggered rollout and synthetic tests that include synchronized control-plane events. Consider adding a control-plane coordination test in CI.
